rationale: Exempt only the two documented HTML-escaping routes. Apply narrow, route-specific checks elsewhere: SQL UNION and tautology structures without treating standalone -- punctuation as malicious; executable HTML markers on the unsafe fragment route; and dot-dot path components, including common encoded forms, on the file route. Ordinary public-readme paths remain permissible. Evaluate this policy, heuristic control, and all LLM proposals at the same CRS paranoia level.
risks: Regex cannot fully parse SQL, HTML, URL decoding, or normalization. SQL comments can split tokens and evade structural matching, while broader comment rules would falsely reject legitimate strings containing -- or comment-like text. Legitimate prose, code examples, event-handler documentation, javascript: text, or paths intentionally containing parent-directory components may still trigger. Alternate encodings, malformed markup, unusual SQLite syntax, double decoding beyond covered forms, absolute paths, symlink behavior, and platform-specific separators may bypass these patterns; the separate restricted compiler must verify supported syntax and matching semantics.
